criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
evidence: Purdue Housing snapshot names FUSE at 720 Northwestern Avenue; Pierce Engineers identifies the matching seven-level project and private housing program.

Independently parsed the saved OSM XML. Way 256639574 is tagged name=FUSE and building=residential. Applying the documented local approximate transform to its 58-point closed ring yields 57 unique plan vertices; they exactly coincide at the saved Blender mesh precision with the 57 z=0 vertices of the retained FUSE shell (computed mean and maximum nearest-vertex errors both 0 at Blender float precision).
The raw OSM XML retains the source feature timestamp. OSM is community-mapped rather than survey-grade, so it corroborates identity and plan but is not a survey certification.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
evidence: Converted OSM bounds X=-107.0479446..-24.5781131 m and Y=561.4959680..643.7988160 m agree with the retained shell bounds X=-107.0479431..-24.5781136 m and Y=561.4959717..643.7988281 m, within coordinate storage precision.
The reopened shell dimensions are 82.4698 x 82.3029 m. Full decorative-geometry bounds and updated manifest bounds include setbacks/signs and are not misrepresented as the structural footprint.

The Mapletree coordinate is explicitly treated as an address pin, not a building centroid, avoiding a false position discrepancy. The geographic conversion is explicitly described as an approximate local transform, not a surveyed CRS.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
evidence: Pierce Engineers source supports one commercial level over two below-grade parking levels and four apartment levels above, seven total. Reopened asset contains the five above-grade levels and concrete slabs/supports extending to z=-6.42 m for a schematic two-level below-grade representation.

The axonometric preview displays four upper window rows over a commercial podium, courtyard opening, split flat roof and parapet. These elements broadly match the sourced program and visible project image.

The shell's 16 m above-grade height is inherited and explicitly unverified; floor heights, roof construction/profile, basement parking grid and ramps are schematic. The saved plan does not establish those vertical dimensions.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
evidence: Reopened model contains repeated window glass/frame bays, brick piers, light spandrels, storefront glazing, double-leaf entrance forms, courtyard-facing windows, and two upper-corner FUSE font signs. Both corner signs are visible in the axonometric preview.

The saved Archilovers page references an exterior photograph with brick/panel treatment, corner composition, storefront and rooftop FUSE identity signs. It documents broad exterior character, not scaled elevations.

Entrances, exact sign placement/size, facade cadence and material divisions remain schematic. Door forms are present but are not legible in the two saved previews; no dimensioned elevation or entrance plan is preserved.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
evidence: Opened the saved .blend in Blender 4.5.15. Asset_massing_fuse_39cf4b5 has 11 objects, matching the current manifest object list and object_count. FUSE retains its original shell; all collection objects have no modifiers. A legacy scene engine warning is emitted on open, but it does not prevent collection inspection.
All four referenced image textures are packed. Collection and asset path remain stable. Dedicated build script and two previews are present.

Evidence JSON includes URLs, providers, feature IDs, retrieval/source dates when available, CRS or non-spatial source designation, method, uncertainty, and local raw snapshots for Purdue Housing, Pierce Engineers, OSM, Mapletree search snippet, and Archilovers. The visual source is represented by a page snapshot and image URL rather than a preserved image file, and no exterior entrance view or verified vertical drawing is included.

Minor inconsistency: the FUSE object's custom source_footprint property says mean deviation 0.000368 m, whereas evidence.json reports 0.0000154 m mean and 0.0000301 m max; independent comparison of the rounded saved Blender vertices produced 0 error at mesh precision. Correct or remove that stale custom-property statistic for a fully consistent record.

evidence.detail: Reopened in Blender 4.5.15; independently inspected collection membership, object count, bounds/dimensions, modifiers, sign objects, basement geometry, and packed images.
Inspected FUSE manifest record; object_count=11 and object list matches reopened collection names.
Reviewed source facts and metadata, geometry measurements, edit claims, uncertainty labels, reopen check and preview paths.
Parsed source way 256639574 by its explicit FUSE/residential tags and independently compared its transformed closed ring to the saved shell z=0 vertices.
Reviewed the raw official residence snapshot for FUSE identity, address, retail, heated parking and courtyard.
Reviewed the saved engineering project page snapshot for seven-level program and reported project area.
Reviewed the saved project-page snapshot for exterior photo reference and source date.
Viewed the saved exterior image; repeated facade, courtyard, parapet and two upper-corner signs are visible.
Viewed the saved plan image; retained near-square ring, courtyard opening, and decorative elements are visible.
Reviewed dedicated build logic for four upper-level window bands, entry forms, two FUSE signs, estimated roof/court and schematic basement levels.

findings: PASS: 8.25/10 meets the repository 8/10 standard. Source-backed plan geometry, campus position, and horizontal dimensions are strongly corroborated by the named OSM FUSE footprint.
The seven-level use program is sourced and represented. Keep the 16 m height, precise floor elevations, roof details, entry locations and basement layout explicitly marked estimated or unverified.

Optional record cleanup: reconcile the custom FUSE source_footprint property (0.000368 m mean) with evidence.json's OSM comparison statistics and the direct saved-mesh comparison; no geometry correction is indicated.
The two previews do not clearly show the entry doors. A street-level entrance view would improve reviewability; available evidence still does not validate their exact locations.
No source-backed evidence establishes survey-grade accuracy, detailed elevations, or exact parking/entrance layouts; those claims should remain limited.
